stem:
Mona has two card angles. She wants to know which is larger by overlaying them.

Which method decides correctly?

options.text: Lay them so the vertices miss each other, and still claim the overlay compares the angles.
Say that the larger angle is what produces a successful overlay, instead of using overlay to compare.
Place both vertices together and match one arm; the angle whose other arm lies outside is larger (they match if equal).
Use the same overlay test to decide which decorative colour on the card is brighter.

teacher.key_rationale: Overlay compares turn only when vertices coincide and one arm is matched. Missing vertices, reversing cause and test, or scoring colour all miss that comparison.
